**Helping Every Child Succeed in Maths: A Change in Our Teaching Approach**

We want to explain an important change in how we teach maths, and why we believe it will help all our students.

**What’s Changing?**
We are moving away from putting students into separate “ability groups” or “streams” (like Set 1, Set 2, Set 3) for their maths lessons. Instead, students will learn together in mixed groups with their classmates.

**Why Are We Making This Change?**

1.  **It Gives Every Child More Time to Understand.** In the old system, once a class moved on from a topic, students who were struggling often didn’t get another chance to fully grasp it. Now, we can spend more time on key ideas, making sure everyone has a solid foundation before moving forward. No one gets left behind.

2.  **It Raises Expectations for Everyone.** Sometimes, being placed in a “lower” group can make a student feel like they’re “just not good at maths.” This can limit how hard they try and what they believe they can achieve. In mixed classes, we see all children rise to the challenge. Students who find maths easier can deepen their understanding by explaining ideas to others, while everyone benefits from higher goals.

3.  **It’s Fairer and More Flexible.** A child’s “ability” isn’t fixed. A student might find fractions tricky but excel at problem-solving. Mixed teaching allows us to see each child’s strengths in different areas and help them where they need it most, rather than giving them a single label.

4.  **It Prepares Them for the Real World.** Life and work don’t separate people into “ability groups.” Learning in a mixed setting helps students learn to collaborate, communicate, and solve problems with people of all different strengths—a vital life skill.

**We Know This Might Sound Worrying**

Many of us remember being in “top” or “bottom” maths sets. You might worry:
*   *“Will the work be too hard for my child if they struggle?”*
*   *“Will the work be too easy and hold back my child if they’re advanced?”*

**Here is our promise for how it will work:**

*   **No One-Size-Fits-All:** Teachers will not teach the same lesson to every student in the same way. They will provide different tasks and support *within* the same classroom. For example, while the class works on multiplication, some might use practical tools, others might solve number problems, and some might tackle complex puzzles—all on the same theme.
*   **Constant Support:** Teachers and teaching assistants will be able to spend more time helping individuals and small groups right there in the lesson.
*   **Regular Check-Ins:** We will closely track every student’s progress. If your child needs extra help or an extra challenge, we will provide it. You will still receive clear updates on how your child is doing.

**Our Goal**
Our goal is simple: to make sure **every single student** leaves our school feeling more confident in maths, believing they can improve with effort, and equipped with the skills they need for their future.

We are happy to talk more about this. Please come to our **Maths Evening** on **[Date]** at **[Time]** in the school hall, where our maths teachers can answer your questions and show you examples of the lessons.

Thank you for your support as we work together for your children’s success.

Sincerely,

The [School Name] Maths Team & Leadership
